correctness.rationale: Minimum triples characterized from the original closed-neighborhood condition, with an independent direct predicate test on 17,224 three-cell placements. Exact edge degrees obtained from disjoint shared-pair completions; edge count by degree sum. Any pair of minimum triples is supported on at most six rows and six columns, allowing a rigorous finite reduction to the 25 auxiliary 2..6 by 2..6 exchange graphs. An exact exhaustive Python verifier checked every vertex has three-step reachability to all others in each of the 25 finite graphs. Two disjoint corner triples prove sharpness. Quantifiers restricted to m,n>=4; finite checking is a genuine bounded-support lemma, not unbounded extrapolation.

evidence: The 2020 Mynhardt–Nasserasr survey describes path/cycle, tree, cograph and Harary jump gamma cases, plus general Johnson-graph embedding. Rall (2021) classifies well-dominated direct products and singles out K_3 × K_3; it does not characterize the present reconfiguration graphs. A distinct ranked finding titled Sharp diameter three for compatible basis pairs in arbitrary rank-3 matroids concerns matroid bases rather than graph domination.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The universal Johnson-graph diameter bound does not pass to induced subgraphs in general. The survey tree bounds and cograph bounds are inapplicable to these graph products, and well-dominatedness does not bound the exchange distance between minimum sets. Matroid basis-pair feasibility and its symmetric exchange operation differ from minimum domination and single-set token jumps.

evidence: The two OEIS records imply the exact number and identity of minimum triples, and are **not** new here. The survey yields the induced-subgraph-of-Johnson-graph property and distinguishes jump from slide. Rall identifies K_3 × K_3 as well-dominated but says nothing about p,q>=4 jump reconfiguration.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: From a known induced vertex family, an explicit edge analysis is still necessary for local degrees, and a path-construction or connectivity proof is necessary for diameter; neither follows from counts or generic Johnson containment. The 25-kernel certificate and double-counting arguments provide the missing implications. Any prior theorem that directly states this diameter or degree structure would override this novelty assessment; none has been found in the material inspected.

evidence: The same graph is the rectangular rook complement and the categorical/tensor/direct product of two complete graphs. OEIS:A292074 and OEIS:A384123 describe minimum sets of this graph but not an exchange graph. arXiv:2003.05956v1, pp. 2-3 and §4.3, defines the jump gamma-graph with adjacency by one replacement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact equivalent formulation asks for the diameter/degree sequence of the induced subgraph of the Johnson graph on corner and three-matching triples. The OEIS results give its vertex set only; no cited text fixes edges or path lengths. Results about slide gamma-graphs impose an additional adjacency restriction and are not equivalent.

value.rationale: Optimal dominating configurations of K_m × K_n admit arbitrary one-cell exchanges, a natural reconfiguration model already studied for other graph families. Despite the state count growing polynomially of total degree six, any two optima are linked by only three moves, and an exact degree split shows a unique regular case m=n=4. This reveals reachability, local flexibility and a sharp structural boundary absent from published minimal-set enumerations; it is not a routine restatement of the known domination number.
